import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.70

by A. N. Fomin

Prove or disprove Cameron's conjecture: if $G$ is a finite primitive permutation group of
subrank $m$, then either the rank of $G$ is bounded by a function of $m$, or the order of a
point stabilizer is at most $m$. The subrank of a transitive permutation group is the maximum
rank of the transitive constituents of a point stabilizer.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 9.70.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.70»

open MulAction

/-- The rank of a permutation group at a point $α$: the number of orbits of the point
stabilizer $G_α$ on the permutation domain. -/
noncomputable def permutationRank (G Ω : Type*) [Group G] [Fintype Ω] [MulAction G Ω]
    (α : Ω) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card (orbitRel.Quotient (stabilizer G α) Ω)

/-- The subrank of a finite permutation group at a point $α$. For each $β$, the orbit
$G_α \cdot β$ is a transitive constituent of $G_α$; its rank is the number of orbits on
$G_α \cdot β$ of the two-point stabilizer $G_{α,β}$. The maximum is unchanged when the
same constituent is indexed by more than one choice of $β$. -/
noncomputable def subrank (G Ω : Type*) [Group G] [Fintype Ω] [MulAction G Ω]
    (α : Ω) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact Finset.univ.sup fun β : Ω ↦
    Nat.card (orbitRel.Quotient (stabilizer (stabilizer G α) β)
      (orbit (stabilizer G α) β))

/--
Prove or disprove Cameron's conjecture: is there a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$
such that, for every $m$, every finite faithful primitive permutation group $G$ on a set
$Ω$ of degree at least two, and every $α \in Ω$, if the subrank at $α$ is $m$, then either
the rank at $α$ is at most $f(m)$ or the order of $G_α$ is at most $m$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.70» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ,
      ∀ (m : ℕ) (G Ω : Type) [Group G] [Fintype G] [Fintype Ω] [MulAction G Ω]
        (α : Ω),
        Nontrivial Ω → FaithfulSMul G Ω → IsPreprimitive G Ω → subrank G Ω α = m →
          permutationRank G Ω α ≤ f m ∨ Nat.card (stabilizer G α) ≤ m := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.70»
modeling_decisions: A finite permutation group is represented by finite types G and Ω, a group structure on G, and a faithful MulAction G Ω.
Mathlib's MulAction.IsPreprimitive supplies transitivity and the absence of nontrivial blocks; Nontrivial Ω enforces the decomposition's implicit degree-at-least-two condition.
The rank at α is the cardinality of the orbit quotient for the action of the point stabilizer G_α on Ω.
The subrank at α is the maximum, over β : Ω, of the number of G_{α,β}-orbits on the G_α-orbit of β. Indexing by all β may duplicate constituents but does not change the maximum.

The bounding function f is quantified once outside all values of m and all finite primitive actions, as required. The base point α is universally quantified; transitivity makes the resulting stabilizer order and ranks independent of that choice.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.70

by A. N. Fomin

Prove or disprove the conjecture of P. Cameron (Bull. London Math. Soc., 13, no. 1 (1981),
1--22): if $G$ is a finite primitive permutation group of subrank $m$, then either the rank
of $G$ is bounded by a function of $m$ or the order of a point stabilizer is at most $m$.
The *subrank* of a transitive permutation group is defined to be the maximum rank of the
transitive constituents of a point stabilizer.

Here the *rank* of a transitive permutation group $G$ on $\Omega$ is the number of orbits of
a point stabilizer $G_\alpha$ on $\Omega$. The *transitive constituents* of $G_\alpha$ are the
transitive permutation groups induced by $G_\alpha$ on its orbits $\Delta \subseteq \Omega$.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), problem 9.70
- [P. J. Cameron, *Finite permutation groups and finite simple groups*, Bull. London Math. Soc.
  13 (1981), 1--22](https://doi.org/10.1112/blms/13.1.1)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.70»

open MulAction

variable (G : Type*) {Ω : Type*} [Group G] [MulAction G Ω]

/-- The rank of a transitive permutation group `G` on `Ω`, computed at the point `α`: the number
of orbits of the point stabilizer $G_\alpha$ on $\Omega$ (including the orbit $\{\alpha\}$).
For a transitive action this number does not depend on the choice of `α`. -/
noncomputable def rank (α : Ω) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card (orbitRel.Quotient (stabilizer G α) Ω)

/-- The subrank of a transitive permutation group `G` on `Ω`, computed at the point `α`: the
maximum of the ranks of the transitive constituents of the point stabilizer $G_\alpha$, i.e. of
the transitive actions of $G_\alpha$ on its orbits $\Delta \subseteq \Omega$ (including the orbit
$\{\alpha\}$). The rank of $G_\alpha$ on the orbit $\Delta$ of a point $\beta$ is the number of
orbits of $G_{\alpha\beta}$ on $\Delta$, so the maximum is taken over all points `β : Ω`.
For a transitive action this number does not depend on the choice of `α`. -/
noncomputable def subrank (α : Ω) : ℕ :=
  ⨆ β : Ω, rank (stabilizer G α) (⟨β, mem_orbit_self β⟩ : orbit (stabilizer G α) β)

variable {G}

/-- The rank of a permutation group on a finite set `Ω` is at most the size of `Ω`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem rank_le_card [Finite Ω] (α : Ω) : rank G α ≤ Nat.card Ω :=
  Nat.card_le_card_of_surjective _ Quotient.mk''_surjective

/-- The rank of a permutation group on a nonempty finite set is at least one. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem one_le_rank [Finite Ω] (α : Ω) : 1 ≤ rank G α :=
  haveI : Nonempty (orbitRel.Quotient (stabilizer G α) Ω) := ⟨⟦α⟧⟩
  Nat.card_pos

/-- The subrank of a permutation group on a finite set `Ω` is at most the size of `Ω`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem subrank_le_card [Finite Ω] (α : Ω) : subrank G α ≤ Nat.card Ω :=
  ciSup_le' fun _ ↦ (rank_le_card _).trans (Nat.card_le_card_of_injective _ Subtype.val_injective)

/-- The subrank of a permutation group on a nonempty finite set is at least one, because of the
transitive constituent of $G_\alpha$ on the orbit $\{\alpha\}$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem one_le_subrank [Finite Ω] (α : Ω) : 1 ≤ subrank G α :=
  le_ciSup_of_le (Set.finite_range _).bddAbove α (one_le_rank _)

/--
Prove or disprove the conjecture of P. Cameron (Bull. London Math. Soc., 13, no. 1 (1981),
1--22): if $G$ is a finite primitive permutation group of subrank $m$, then either the rank
of $G$ is bounded by a function of $m$ or the order of a point stabilizer is at most $m$.

Formally: is there a function $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every finite
primitive permutation group $G$ on a set $\Omega$ with point stabilizer $G_\alpha$, either
$\operatorname{rank}(G) \le f(\operatorname{subrank}(G))$ or $|G_\alpha| \le
\operatorname{subrank}(G)$? By transitivity, the rank, the subrank and the order of a point
stabilizer do not depend on the choice of the point $\alpha$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.70» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ (Ω : Type) [Finite Ω] (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω)) [IsPreprimitive G Ω]
      (α : Ω), rank G α ≤ f (subrank G α) ∨ Nat.card (stabilizer G α) ≤ subrank G α := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.70»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.70

by A. N. Fomin

Prove or disprove Cameron's conjecture: if $G$ is a finite primitive
permutation group of subrank $m$, then either the rank of $G$ is bounded by a
function of $m$, or the order of a point stabilizer is at most $m$.

The subrank of a transitive permutation group is the maximum rank of the
transitive constituents of a point stabilizer.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46),
Problem 9.70.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.70»

/-- The rank of a finite permutation group at a point $\alpha$ is the number
of orbits of the stabilizer $G_\alpha$ on the permutation domain. -/
noncomputable def permutationRank (G Ω : Type*) [Group G] [MulAction G Ω]
    [Fintype Ω] (α : Ω) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card (MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient (MulAction.stabilizer G α) Ω)

/-- The subrank at $\alpha$ is the maximum, over the $G_\alpha$-orbits
$\Delta$, of the rank of the transitive constituent $G_\alpha \curvearrowright
\Delta$. Equivalently, the maximum may be taken over all $\beta$: the relevant
constituent has domain $\Delta = G_\alpha \cdot \beta$, and its rank is the
number of $G_{\alpha,\beta}$-orbits on $\Delta$. -/
noncomputable def subrank (G Ω : Type*) [Group G] [MulAction G Ω]
    [Fintype Ω] (α : Ω) : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.sup fun β : Ω ↦
    Nat.card (MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient
      (MulAction.stabilizer (MulAction.stabilizer G α) β)
      (MulAction.orbit (MulAction.stabilizer G α) β))

/--
Prove or disprove Cameron's conjecture: there is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to
\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $m$ and every finite faithful primitive
permutation group $G$ of degree at least two and subrank $m$, either the rank of
$G$ is at most $f(m)$ or the order of a point stabilizer is at most $m$.

Here the rank is the number of $G_\alpha$-orbits on the permutation domain.
The subrank is the maximum, including the constituent $\{\alpha\}$, of the
ranks of the transitive constituents of $G_\alpha$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.70» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ,
      ∀ (m : ℕ) (G Ω : Type) [Group G] [Fintype G] [Fintype Ω]
        [MulAction G Ω] [FaithfulSMul G Ω],
        2 ≤ Fintype.card Ω → MulAction.IsPreprimitive G Ω →
          ∀ α : Ω, subrank G Ω α = m →
            permutationRank G Ω α ≤ f m ∨
              Nat.card (MulAction.stabilizer G α) ≤ m := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.70»
modeling_decisions: A finite permutation group is represented by a finite abstract group with a finite faithful `MulAction` on the permutation domain.
Primitivity is represented by `MulAction.IsPreprimitive`; the explicit degree bound `2 ≤ Fintype.card Ω` excludes the degenerate degree-zero and degree-one actions.
Rank and subrank are based at a quantified point α. For a primitive (hence transitive) action these values, and the point-stabilizer order, are independent of the chosen point.
The uniform bounding function `f : ℕ → ℕ` is quantified outside `m`, the group, and its action, while the two alternatives remain a disjunction for each group.

The maximum defining subrank is indexed by every β in the domain rather than by orbit representatives. Points in the same point-stabilizer orbit yield the same constituent rank, so repetitions do not change the maximum; β = α includes the singleton constituent.
